label: negative
description: The zero-address guard on newBeneficiary is rewritten from require(newBeneficiary != address(0), "...") to a custom error: if (newBeneficiary == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress(). Same condition on the same parameter, different (gas-cheaper) form.
why_labeled: Exclusion 6.5: the check was replaced by an equivalent custom error with the same condition - a semantic equivalence, not a text match. require(x != 0) and if (x == 0) revert are the same guard: both revert exactly when newBeneficiary is the zero address, before the state write. A text-diff rule would see the require vanish and false-positive; a semantic comparison must recognise the negated-condition custom-error form as the same validation. Rule 6 MUST stay quiet.
